methods.rates: 95% Wilson intervals; errors excluded from win-rate denominators and audited separately.
methods.paired: Same first 54 index values per party size and difficulty, seed and exact ordered hero roster. Paired difference normal interval with Wilson zero-event floor, matching statistics.ts.
methods.timeouts: Combat draw at 100 rounds; 100-minute deadline during a live battle; deadline between battles; unexplained cases flagged.
methods.duration: Minutes are simulated game time including actual presentation event duration; >90 is a strict comparison. Winning duration is conditional on victory.
methods.labels: Victory requires four defeated stages, living hero and at least 80 minutes. Non-victory with all stages defeated and survivors is flagged. A defeat with a survivor is flagged.
methods.aggregateUncertainty: Difficulty rows are primary. Overall aggregates combine paired difficulties and heterogeneous compositions; their Wilson intervals are descriptive and do not account for that clustering.

limitations: Held-out seeds assess this deterministic combat policy and scripted route, not human win probability. No human navigation, simultaneous split groups, roaming reinforcements, connection delay or decision time.
The party stays together, prefers normal encounters, follows the radial route, and uses generated campfires and a greedy gear/skill policy. Changing those decisions can materially change success.
Difficulty comparisons reuse seeds and party rosters. Aggregate observations across difficulties are correlated; use per-difficulty intervals and paired differences.
Per-hero solo samples are 14 campaigns per difficulty. Wide intervals and multiple comparisons prevent a precise hero balance ranking.
The starter control also forbids learned skills, so its contrast measures the combined benefit of progression equipment and skills, not equipment alone.
Zero wins in a finite control sample is not proof of impossibility. Control and progression routes can diverge after combat timing, injuries and equipment choices change.
The experiment stops at 100 simulated minutes and combat at 100 rounds. Timeout outcomes include stalemates and deadline censorship, not automatic player deaths.
Successful-duration summaries exclude defeats, escapes and timeouts; they cannot be read as the average length of every run.
validationRole: Second independent holdout, candidate4, fresh balance-holdout-v2 seeds. Reported after configuration was frozen; first holdout is historical observed data.

calibrationAssessment.interpretation: Compatibility means the target intersects a 95% Wilson interval; it does not prove equality or statistical equivalence. No equivalence margin was prespecified.

duration.interpretation: Descriptive runtime target, not a demand that every run fall inside the range or that most runs exceed 90 minutes.
